# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 8 (Bu-Vb Ss8)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Duṭṭhadosa Sikkhāpada* constitutes the eighth rule of the *Saṅghādisesa* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a monk who, motivated by anger and malice, makes an unfounded accusation against another monk concerning an offense entailing expulsion (*pārājika*) is subject to formal suspension (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. The rule's origin story centers on the figure of Dabba the Mallian (*Dabba Mallaputta*), a venerable monk who attained arahantship at the age of seven and served the saṅgha by assigning lodgings and apportioning meals [SuttaCentral].
This rule corresponds to parallel provisions across all major surviving Vinaya traditions, including the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, Vibhaṅgas, and Parivāra of the Theravāda, as well as the Vinayas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. At the passage level, SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree in identifying an extensive parallel within the Pali canon itself: Kd 14 (*Samathakkhandhaka*), which shares substantial text verbatim (§1.1.1–1.9.26 with §4.1.1–4.9.27) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also reveals massive internal text reuse with the immediately subsequent rule, *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 9* (over 44,000 shared characters), as well as significant matches across other Khandhaka sections (Kd 16, Kd 15, Kd 8, Kd 6, Kd 11, Kd 19) and Vinaya exegesis, including the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā*, and the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus also record correspondences with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* and Sanskrit Vinaya texts such as the *Śayanāsanavastu* and *Poṣadhasthāpanavastu* [DharmaNexus]. Complete translations into modern languages include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
